issues.legal_issue: An uncorrected entry recording a subtenant in the relevant historical land record makes that subtenant an occupant entitled to the statutory land rights, without inquiry into when the subtenancy began or whether an earlier adjudication found no subletting.
material_facts: The claimants were recorded as subtenants in the land records for the relevant year.
An earlier ejectment suit had found no subletting and held that the entries showing subtenancy were incorrect.
The entry for the relevant year was not corrected; a village official later removed entries for a different year but lacked authority to alter the relevant year's entry.
The claimants sought possession under the land-reform statute, and the Board of Revenue allowed their claims.
issues.conclusion: The relevant year's uncorrected entry had to be accepted. As between a tenant and a subtenant, the recorded subtenant was the occupant entitled to the statutory rights, and no inquiry into when the subtenancy arose was required.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 20(b)(i) of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1952, a person recorded as an occupant in the specified year's Khasra or Khatauni could acquire adhivasi rights. Explanations II and III provided for a corrected entry, including one deemed corrected by a final court order or decree, to prevail. The Court applied The Upper Ganges Sugar Mills Ltd. v. Khalil-ul-Rahman, [1961] 1 S.C.R. 564; Amba Prasad v. Abdul Noor Khan, [1964] 7 S.C.R. 800; Ram Dular Singh v. Babu Sukh Ram, [1963] A.L.J. 667; and Nanakchand v. Board of Revenue, U.P., [1955] A.L.J. 408. Those authorities establish that the statutory scheme relies on the specified historical record and avoids renewed inquiry into disputed possession; as between tenant and subtenant, the latter may be the recorded occupant.

rule.if: statutory_land_possession_claim and appeal_from_revenue_board_decision and claimant_recorded_as_subtenant and relevant_historical_entry_uncorrected

predicates.statutory_land_possession_claim: A claimant sought possession or a related land right under a statutory land-reform scheme based on a historical land record.
predicates.appeal_from_revenue_board_decision: A party appealed a court decision concerning a revenue board's ruling on the statutory land claim.
predicates.claimant_recorded_as_subtenant: The relevant historical land record identified the claimant as a subtenant under a tenant.
predicates.relevant_historical_entry_uncorrected: The entry for the relevant historical year was not corrected by the applicable cutoff, including by a final order or decree treated as a correction.
predicates.recorded_subtenant_qualifies_as_occupant: A claimant recorded as a subtenant qualifies as the occupant for the statutory land right.

issues.definition: When a statutory land-possession claim is appealed from a revenue-board decision, and the claimant is recorded as a subtenant in an uncorrected relevant historical entry, the claimant qualifies as the occupant for the statutory land right.

issues.legal_issue: A procedural objection that was not raised before the revenue board need not be examined on appeal.
material_facts: The appellants argued that the claimants' applications were defective because they did not state the dates of dispossession, as required by a procedural rule.
The objection had not been raised before the Board of Revenue.
issues.conclusion: The Court did not examine the objection because it had not been canvassed before the Board of Revenue.
issues.legal_principle: The Court declined to consider the objection under rule 183 of the rules framed under the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act because it had not been raised before the Board of Revenue.

predicates.appeal_from_revenue_board_decision: A party appealed a court decision concerning a revenue board's ruling.
predicates.procedural_objection_not_raised_before_b: A party raised a procedural objection on appeal that it had not presented to the revenue board.
predicates.procedural_objection_left_unexamined_on_: The procedural objection is not examined on appeal.

issues.definition: In an appeal from a revenue-board decision, a procedural objection not raised before the board is left unexamined on appeal.
